metrics.precedent_match: Exact match to Durham method: (Bicycle + On foot) / all residents in employment INCLUDING 'Work mainly at or from home'. 2011 denominator = 'All categories' minus 'Not in employment' (16-74 universe). 2021 universe = all usual residents 16+ in employment the week before the census.
metrics.caveats: There is no combined-authority (E47000001) geography for TS061 or QS701EW in Nomis. I used two published geographies that cover exactly the 10 boroughs: for 2011, the former metropolitan county 'Greater Manchester (Met County)' E11000001 (Nomis TYPE462), and for 2021, the 'Greater Manchester' LEP E37000015 (Nomis TYPE459, as of April 2021). Both match the sum of the 10 boroughs' counts exactly, for every category; I cross-checked them against TYPE464 (2011) and TYPE154 (2021). So the numerator, denominator and ratio are identical whether taken from the GM geography or as a sum of 10 boroughs. Census 2021 was taken on 21 March 2021, during a COVID lockdown. Working from home was 28.6% of the 2021 denominator against 3.9% in 2011, so the share including WFH falls (12.58 to 9.38), while the share excluding WFH is flat (13.09 to 13.14). Census counts are statistically disclosure-controlled (2021 cell perturbation), so tiny differences from other aggregations are possible.

metrics.precedent_match: Durham used ONS ad hoc 008005 (single-authority means, 2015 and 2016). GM has no single published mean.
metrics.unavailable_reason: I searched two ONS ad hoc releases. (1) ONS ad hoc 008005 (LFS TRVTME, OD2007 to OD2016) publishes mean one-way minutes only by individual local authority (UALA/LAUA). The 2015 sheet uses old county/district codes (BL Bolton ... BW Wigan) and the 2016 sheet uses E08000001-E08000010. It has no Greater Manchester or metropolitan-county row; North West appears only at region level in some sheets. (2) ONS ad hoc 010202 (OD2018) likewise publishes means for the 10 boroughs individually (for example Manchester 30.36, Tameside 33.88, Rochdale 22.58) with no GM row and no weights. In 008005 the only possible weights are weighted counts by travel mode per borough, and 27-31 of those cells per year are suppressed ('*', sample too small). A GM mean weighted by commuters would therefore have to treat suppressed cells as zero or impute them, which takes researcher judgment. As a rough check, treating '*' as 0 gives about 28.05 (2015) and 29.39 (2016). Averaging the borough means is prohibited, and ONS warns the estimates rest on small samples. No other ONS, DfT (NTS is national or regional only) or TfGM source publishes a GM-level mean commute time. The TfGM TRADS survey reports trip lengths, not a commute-time mean comparable to the LFS.
metrics.caveats: If the founder wants a GM figure, the defensible route is a custom ONS request for an LFS TRVTME mean on a Greater Manchester (E11000001 or E47000001) geography. I did not use the suppressed-cell weighted estimates.

metrics.precedent_match: Durham is unavailable because no measured length of dedicated network exists for County Durham. For GM, TfGM publishes a measured, typed cycle-route GIS layer, which Durham lacks. The founder may still prefer 'unavailable' for UK comparability; see caveats.
metrics.caveats: Value = length of 'dedicated' categories in TfGM's GM Cycle Routes open data, using only routes with status 'open for use' in the archived editions: RouteType 11 'On-road route with physical segregation e.g. armadillos' plus RouteType 5 'Traffic-free routes, e.g. converted railway line'. Lengths were computed from British National Grid polyline geometry. For the 2026 edition, my geometric total (1,716.7 km) matches TfGM's own 'length' field (1,716.68 km), which validates the method. EXCLUDED and reported separately: canal towpaths (codes 6/7), quiet/advisory on-road routes (1/2), on-road painted lanes and advanced stop lines (code 3), footpaths where cyclists walk (9), and code 4. Code 3 has about 320 km in every edition; the 2026 edition relabels it 'On road route - light segregation', but TfGM's own code definition is 'cycle lanes and/or advanced stop lines', so I did not treat it as protected. Code 4 mixes segregated tracks with shared-use footways and is labelled 'shared use footways' in 2026. Including it would add 57-144 mi. Material caveats: (1) This is map data supplied by the 10 councils. TfGM says it 'cannot be guaranteed to be fully correct', so year-to-year change mixes construction with mapping corrections. (2) About 35-43% of the traffic-free length is coded 'very rough unpaved surface, suitable for mountain bike use only'. Each row's notes give the figure without it. (3) Editions are irregular (Jun 2015, Jun 2016, Jun 2017, Nov 2018, Sep 2022, Mar 2026), so 2019-2021 and 2023-2025 have no data. (4) TfGM's headline Bee Network figure is a different concept and NOT used here: 117 km Dec 2024, 133 km Jul 2025, 161 km Dec 2025 of 'Bee Network standard' routes, delivered by the Active Travel Programme since 2018/19. The Jan 2026 Active Travel Annual Report (para 2.15) says that standard includes 'quieter residential or vehicle restricted streets and off-road greenways' and crossings/junctions. It also counts programme delivery only, not the whole network, and the series is internally inconsistent (Oct 2024 BNC paper '>120km', Annual Report '117km as of Dec 2024'). No DfT or Active Travel England dataset gives a cycle-network length by local authority.

metrics.precedent_match: Durham definition: route-miles of NEW Metrolink/rail line or dedicated BRT corridor entering revenue service per calendar year. A new stop on existing track = 0, and on-highway bus lanes are not counted as dedicated corridor. Durham used source-backed zeros, estimated.
metrics.caveats: Openings 2015-2025: (a) Metrolink Second City Crossing (2CC) phase 1, Victoria to Exchange Square, opened 6 Dec 2015. VolkerRail (contractor) gives a 0.6 km stretch. (b) Leigh-Salford-Manchester busway, guided section Leigh-Tyldesley-Ellenbrook, opened 3 Apr 2016. TfGM, quoted in Transport Network on 30 Mar 2016, gives a 4.5 mile bus-only guideway; a 2020 Vantage upgrade document gives 7.5 km. The roughly 13.5 km of on-highway bus lanes (A580 East Lancs Road, Salford/Manchester) is excluded as not a dedicated corridor. Counting the 21 km of 'segregated bus measures' would give 13.0 mi in 2016. (c) 2CC full line, St Peter's Square to Exchange Square, opened 26 Feb 2017. VolkerRail gives 1.3 km for the 2CC, which I read as the whole 2CC, so 2017 = 1.3 - 0.6 = 0.7 km. That split is my judgment: if 1.3 km is the 2017 increment alone, 2017 = 0.81 mi. (d) Metrolink Trafford Park Line, Pomona to Trafford Centre, opened 22 Mar 2020: 5.5 km per the EIB project page and Railway Gazette. Corroboration: DfT LRT0203 Metrolink route km as at 31 March is 92 (2015), 96 (2016), 97 (2017-2019), 103 (2020-2026). The FY2019-20 +6 km matches the TPL. Whole-km rounding and possible remeasurement make the FY2015-16 +4 km unreliable for small increments. The GMCA 21 Feb 2020 Metrolink report says the network is 'just under 100 km', expanding to 102.5 km with the TPL. EXCLUDED heavy rail: Ordsall Chord, a new approx. 300-350 m Network Rail link, in passenger service from 10 Dec 2017 (+0.19-0.22 mi if heavy rail is in scope). The task scope was Metrolink/BRT, but the Durham definition says 'new rail'. Zero years rest on the flat DfT LRT0203 route-km series (no Metrolink additions Mar 2020 to Mar 2026) and on finding no other guided busway or segregated BRT opening in GMCA/TfGM reporting. Lengths are as published, not GIS-measured.

verdicts.batch: Greater Manchester: Transit and Public Safety (new metrics plus re-sourcing proposals). Adversarial verification, 2026-10-11

issues: I re-pulled both Nomis tables and re-summed all 10 boroughs myself. For TS061 (TYPE154) and QS701EW (TYPE464), all 10 boroughs were present with no suppression, and every category sum equals the GM geography row (E37000015 LEP 2021, E11000001 Met County 2011).
The method matches the Durham precedent exactly: WFH is included in the denominator, and the 2011 universe is total minus 'Not in employment'. The source name matches the precedent string. OGL v3.
Period convention (year, YYYY-01-01) is fine. Keep the lockdown caveat; the 2011 to 2021 fall is driven by WFH.

REFUTED: the claim that ONS ad hoc 008005 'has no Greater Manchester or metropolitan-county row' is wrong. Sheet '2014' (OD 2014, weighted PWT17, variable UALA) is published on a county geography. Row 44 reads '50 Greater Manchester Met County', and its Mean column is 28.678661070858748 minutes. This is a single ONS-published GM-level mean (Met County = the 10 GMCA boroughs), not an average of borough means, so no researcher judgment is involved.

For 2015 and 2016 (the sheets Durham used), the researcher is right. The 2015 sheet lists only boroughs under old codes (e.g. 'BN Manchester'), and the 2016 sheet lists only E08 districts. Neither has a GM row. Sheets 2007 to 2013 and ad hoc 010202 (OD2018) also have no GM row (only 'BN Manchester'). I confirmed both by searching every sheet.

Period caveat: OD2014 falls before the 2015 target window. It is the only GM-level mean ONS publishes. If the founder applies the 2015+ window strictly, the metric reverts to unavailable for 2015 onward for the reasons the researcher gave (no GM row; weighting borough means needs suppressed cells imputed).

Comparability with Durham: the same 2014 sheet carries '20 Durham' = 24.10 min. Adding 2014 to Durham's series would give both jurisdictions an OD2014 point. Durham's 2015/2016 values come from the same file and method.
ONS warns the estimates rest on small samples and should be treated with caution. The table is Crown copyright under OGL v3, so commercial reuse is permitted.

metrics.corrected_notes: Only one GM-level value exists (OD2014, 28.68 min). It sits one year before the target window; include it only if the founder accepts a pre-2015 point. For 2015 onward the honest status stays unavailable, as the researcher argued.

issues: The arithmetic re-derives exactly. I parsed every shapefile myself. Code 5 + code 11 (status 3 only) gives 726.7 / 791.7 / 796.8 / 834.1 / 883.0 km for 2015 / 2016 / 2017 / 2018 / 2022. 2026 (no status field) gives 810.9 + 78.4 = 889.4 km, and the length field agrees at 889.38. The rejection is on concept and consistency, not arithmetic.

CONCEPT: by TfGM's own code definitions, code 5 'Traffic-free routes' includes surface code 1, 'Very rough unpaved surface, suitable for mountain bike use only'. That is 35-43% of the headline (e.g. 348.0 of 810.9 km in 2026). Code 4 is defined as 'Segregated cycle lanes / Shared Use Footways adjacent to the carriageway' and was excluded wholesale. So the figure overcounts (mountain-bike tracks) and undercounts (segregated tracks inside code 4), and the cut depends on researcher judgment.

SERIES INCONSISTENCY (spatial check, 2022 vs 2026): about 24.4 km of code-5 segments that had RouteStatus 0 (undefined, excluded from the 2015-2022 rows) appear as code 5 in the 2026 edition, which has no status field. So do about 2.6 km of status-2 'potential' code-5 routes and about 4.5 km of status-1 'vague idea' code-11 routes. The 2026 row is therefore not like-for-like with earlier rows.

MAPPING CHURN: of the 55.1 km of open code-11 lanes in 2022, only about 37.9 km is still coded 11 in 2026. About 12.3 km now sits under another code and about 9.8 km has no 2026 feature nearby. Code-5 open length falls by 17 km between 2022 and 2026. Year-to-year change reflects recoding by the 10 councils, not construction. TfGM says the data 'cannot be guaranteed to be fully correct'.
Minor inconsistency: the 2026 'excluding very rough' figure removes 348.0 km of code 5 but leaves 2.9 km of very-rough code 11.

Durham precedent: unavailable because no measured length of dedicated network exists. The GM layer is a council-supplied map layer of mixed-quality routes, not a measured dedicated network, and nothing comparable exists for Durham. The Bee Network km series is a different concept, as the researcher correctly said. Under the 'never force-fit, prefer an honest gap' rule, mark this unavailable.

If the founder nonetheless wants a number, the least-bad option is a single 2026 snapshot labelled estimated and defined explicitly as 'TfGM cycle-map length, traffic-free (excluding very-rough surface) plus physically segregated on-road'. That is (810.9 - 348.0 + 75.6) km = about 334.7 mi. Do not use it as a time series.
metrics.corrected_notes: Unavailable: no source measures the length of dedicated cycle infrastructure for the GMCA area. The TfGM GM Cycle Routes open-data layer is council-supplied map data of mixed route quality. About 40% of its 'traffic-free' length is coded mountain-bike-only surface, and segregated tracks are mixed with shared-use footways in code 4. Editions are inconsistent in status coding: the 2026 edition has no status field and includes routes previously coded undefined, potential or concept. Year-to-year change mostly reflects recoding.
